placements.title: Absence Manufactured as History
placements.frame: When a directive commands forgetting or erasing a named subject, did that subject ever hold a place in the record, or does the directive itself construct the absence and then assert it as settled history?
placements.why: Both existing strata and existing graph structure are empty for this repo, and the served nodes (ns__Decision_KnowledgeMapping, ns__Actor_XenaGithubber) name a knowledge-mapping strategy and consultant but hold nothing about any instrument, calibration, or erasure directive — so no existing leaf can be reused (rule 1/4). The settled bindings confirm the Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove have zero prior presence anywhere navigable, and the position pass already reads all three segments as one directional act: two unhedged imperatives commanding erasure (src-1, src-2) capped by a flat declarative retroactively asserting non-occurrence (src-3, 'The observatory never calibrated it'). Per the grain test, the specific spectrograph is not itself a leaf-worthy subject (that would be minting a fact), but the pattern these segments jointly perform — a directive to erase knowledge of something absent, followed by an assertion manufacturing that absence as historical fact — is a subject future envelopes in a knowledge-mapping/organizational-diagnostics repo could plausibly keep feeding (denial, revisionism, or knowledge-suppression as a recurring organizational dynamic). No hub or strata name fits this content even loosely, so it stands as a standalone leaf per rule 6's NEW case rather than being forced under an unrelated parent.
